en: The Sūtra on the Elder’s Reward for Giving, Spoken by the Buddha.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heavens, the Court Proclaimed Grandee, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master of the Transmission of the Teaching, the Subject Fǎtiān, in accordance with the Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, there was a householder named Anāthapiṇḍada who came to where the Buddha was, prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, and sat down to one side.
The Buddha told the householder:

"If there is another person who gives excellent food and drink as a gift in accordance with the Dharma—whether giving with their own hands or giving at all times—they will not obtain vast karmic rewards."
What do you think?
It is because that person’s mind seeks wealth, honor, and happiness.

Furthermore, if there is someone who, without seeking clothing, food, bedding, wealth, honor, or happiness, gives excellent food and drink as a gift in accordance with the Dharma, they shall obtain great wealth, as well as a wife, children, male and female servants, and a retinue who are filial, obedient, and attentive in their service.
"What do you think?
Is it because that person practices giving for the sake of all sentient beings?
The Buddha said:

“Householder! In a past age, there was a brahmin householder named Mīḷha who held a great sacrificial assembly; he practiced giving by filling eighty thousand golden plates with gold dust and bestowing them as alms, and again, he practiced giving by filling eighty thousand silver plates with silver dust and bestowing them as alms.”
Furthermore, he practiced giving by filling eighty thousand golden plates with silver filings;
he practiced giving by filling eighty thousand silver plates with gold filings;
and he practiced giving by filling eighty thousand copper plates with various kinds of exquisite and delicious foods and drinks.
Furthermore, he practiced giving by offering eighty thousand milch cows;
furthermore, he practiced giving by offering eighty thousand young maidens, adorned with exquisite garments, pearls, necklaces, and various ornaments;
furthermore, he practiced giving by offering eighty thousand couches made of gold, silver, ivory, and wood, upon which were spread various fine and delicate rugs and cushions.
Furthermore, he gave as alms eighty thousand palanquins, carriages, and vehicles, all spread with white cotton cloth and Kāśika garments, and adorned with various ornaments.
The Buddha said, “Householder!
The fruit obtained by someone who gives food and drink to a single person of right view surpasses the fruit obtained by that King Mīḷha through such acts of giving as he performed.
"What do you think?
It is because this person does not fall into wrong views.
The Buddha said:

“Householder! That Mīḷhama’s practice of giving in this manner does not equal that of someone who gives food and drink to a single person of right view; nor does it equal giving to a hundred people of right view, for the fruit and reward obtained from the latter surpasses the fruit and reward of the former.”
The Buddha said: "Householder!

That Mīḷhama’s practice of giving is not equal to someone giving food and drink to a single person of right view; one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred people of right view; and giving to a hundred people of right view is not equal to giving to a single *srotāpanna*, for the fruit of retribution obtained from the latter surpasses the fruit of retribution of the former."
The Buddha said, “Householder!

That Mīramā’s practice of giving is not equal to someone giving food and drink to a single person of right view; one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred persons of right view; a hundred persons of right view are not equal to giving to a single *srotāpanna*; and one *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to a hundred *srotāpannas*, for the fruit and reward obtained from the latter surpasses the fruit and reward of the former.”
The Buddha said, “Householder!

That Mīḷhama’s practice of giving is not equal to someone giving food and drink to a single person of right view; one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred people of right view; a hundred people of right view are not equal to giving to a single *srotāpanna*; one *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to a hundred *srotāpannas*; and a hundred *srotāpannas* are not equal to giving to a single *anāgāmin*, for the fruit of retribution obtained from the latter surpasses that of the former.”

The Buddha said, “Householder! That Mīḷhama’s practice of giving is not equal to someone giving food and drink to a single person of right view; giving to one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred persons of right view; giving to a hundred persons of right view is not equal to giving to a single *srotāpanna*; giving to a single *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to a hundred *srotāpannas*; giving to a hundred *srotāpannas* is not equal to giving to a single *anāgāmin*; and giving to a single *anāgāmin* is not equal to giving to a hundred *anāgāmins*, for the fruit and reward obtained from the latter surpasses that of the former.”

The Buddha said, "Householder! That Mīḷha’s practice of giving is not equal to someone giving food and drink to a single person of right view; giving to one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred persons of right view; giving to a hundred persons of right view is not equal to giving to a single *srotāpanna*; giving to a single *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to a hundred *srotāpannas*; giving to a hundred *srotāpannas* is not equal to giving to a single *anāgāmin*; giving to a single *anāgāmin* is not equal to giving to a hundred *anāgāmins*; giving to a hundred *anāgāmins* is not equal to giving to a single *arhat*. The fruit of retribution obtained from the latter is superior to the fruit of retribution of the former."

The Buddha said, “Householder! That Mīḷha’s practice of giving is not equal to someone giving food and drink to a single person of right view; one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred persons of right view; a hundred persons of right view are not equal to giving to a single *srotāpanna*; one *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to a hundred *srotāpannas*; a hundred *srotāpannas* are not equal to giving to a single *anāgāmin*; one *anāgāmin* is not equal to giving to a hundred *anāgāmins*; a hundred *anāgāmins* are not equal to giving to a single *arhat*; and one *arhat* is not equal to giving to a hundred *arhats*. The fruit of retribution obtained from the latter is superior to the fruit of retribution of the former.”

The Buddha said, "Householder! The merit gained by Mīḷha giving such gifts as these does not equal that of someone who gives food and drink to a single person of right view; one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred persons of right view; a hundred persons of right view are not equal to giving to a single *srotāpanna*; one *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to a hundred *srotāpannas*; a hundred *srotāpannas* are not equal to giving to a single *anāgāmin*; one *anāgāmin* is not equal to giving to a hundred *anāgāmins*; a hundred *anāgāmins* are not equal to giving to a single *arhat*; one *arhat* is not equal to giving to a hundred *arhats*; and a hundred *arhats* are not equal to giving to a single *pratyekabuddha*, for the fruit of retribution obtained from the latter surpasses the fruit of retribution of the former."

The Buddha said, “Householder! That Mīramā’s practice of giving is not equal to someone giving food and drink to a single person of right view; one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred people of right view; a hundred people of right view are not equal to giving to a single *srotāpanna*; one *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to a hundred *srotāpannas*; a hundred *srotāpannas* are not equal to giving to a single *anāgāmin*; one *anāgāmin* is not equal to giving to a hundred *anāgāmins*; a hundred *anāgāmins* are not equal to giving to a single *arhat*; one *arhat* is not equal to giving to a hundred *arhats*; a hundred *arhats* are not equal to giving to a single *pratyekabuddha*; and one *pratyekabuddha* is not equal to giving to a hundred *pratyekabuddhas*, for the fruit of reward obtained is superior to the former rewards.”
The Buddha said, “Householder!
That Mīḷhama’s practice of giving is not equal to that of someone who gives food and drink to a single *samyag-gata* (one who has gone rightly).”
When seeing people, giving to one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred people of right view;
giving to a hundred people of right view is not equal to giving to one *srotāpanna*; giving to one *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to a hundred *srotāpannas*;
giving to a hundred *srotāpannas* is not equal to giving to one *anāgāmin*; giving to one *anāgāmin* is not equal to giving to a hundred *anāgāmins*.
Anāgāmins: one hundred Anāgāmins are not equal to giving to one Arhat; one Arhat is not equal to giving to one hundred Arhats;
one hundred Arhats are not equal to giving to one Pratyekabuddha; one Pratyekabuddha is not equal to giving to one hundred Pratyekabuddhas;
one hundred Pratyekabuddhas are not equal to giving to one Tathāgata, Arhat...
“The fruit and retribution obtained from a Perfectly Enlightened One surpasses the fruit and retribution obtained previously.
The Buddha said, “Householder!”
The almsgiving performed by that King Mīḷha is not equal to someone giving food and drink to a single person of right view;
one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred persons of right view; a hundred persons of right view are not equal to giving to a single *srotāpanna*;
one *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to a hundred *srotāpannas*; a hundred...
Giving to a single *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to one *anāgāmin*; giving to one *anāgāmin* is not equal to giving to a hundred *anāgāmins*;
giving to a hundred *anāgāmins* is not equal to giving to one *arhat*; giving to one *arhat* is not equal to giving to a hundred *arhats*;
giving to a hundred *arhats* is not equal to giving to a single *pratyekabuddha*. One *pratyekabuddha*...
Awakening is not as meritorious as giving to a hundred pratyekabuddhas; giving to a hundred pratyekabuddhas is not as meritorious as giving to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha;

and giving to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is not as meritorious as giving to the Buddha and his retinue of great bhikṣus, for the fruit and retribution obtained from this latter gift surpasses those preceding fruits.
The Buddha said, "Householder!
That Mīḷhama’s practice of giving is not equal to that of someone who gives food and drink to a single person of right view."
Regarding the sight of persons: giving to one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred persons of right view;
giving to a hundred persons of right view is not equal to giving to one *srotāpanna*; giving to one *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to a hundred *srotāpannas*;
giving to a hundred *srotāpannas* is not equal to giving to one *anāgāmin*; giving to one *anāgāmin* is not equal to giving to a hundred *anāgāmins*.
One hundred *anāgāmins* are not equal to giving to one *arhat*; one *arhat* is not equal to giving to one hundred *arhats*;
one hundred *arhats* are not equal to giving to one *pratyekabuddha*; one *pratyekabuddha* is not equal to giving to one hundred *pratyekabuddhas*;
and one hundred *pratyekabuddhas* are not equal to giving to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
O Samyaksaṃbuddha, giving to a Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha is not as meritorious as giving to the Buddha and the great assembly of bhikṣus who follow him;
and giving to the Buddha and the great assembly of bhikṣus who follow him is not as meritorious as giving food to all the bowl-holding monks throughout the four quarters,
for the fruit and reward obtained from the latter surpasses those of the former.
The Buddha said, "Householder!
That Mīḷhamā’s practice of giving is not equal to that of someone who gives food and drink to a single person of right view."
Regarding the sight of persons: giving to one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred persons of right view;
giving to a hundred persons of right view is not equal to giving to one *srotāpanna*; giving to one *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to a hundred *srotāpannas*;
giving to a hundred *srotāpannas* is not equal to giving to one *anāgāmin*; giving to one *anāgāmin* is not equal to giving to a hundred *anāgāmins*.
One hundred *anāgāmins* are not equal to giving to one *arhat*; one *arhat* is not equal to giving to one hundred *arhats*;
one hundred *arhats* are not equal to giving to one *pratyekabuddha*; one *pratyekabuddha* is not equal to giving to one hundred *pratyekabuddhas*;
and one hundred *pratyekabuddhas* are not equal to giving to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Giving to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha who has attained equal enlightenment is not as meritorious as giving to the Buddha and the great assembly of bhikṣus following him;
giving to the Buddha and the great assembly of bhikṣus following him is not as meritorious as giving food to all the bowl-holding monks of the four quarters;
and giving food to all the bowl-holding monks of the four quarters is not as meritorious as giving to a single [monk] of the four quarters...
"By dedicating these to the monastic groves of the Saṃgha, the karmic fruit obtained will be superior to the previous fruit.
The Buddha said, "Householder!"
The almsgiving performed by that Mīramā is not equal to someone giving food and drink to a single person of right view;
giving to one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred persons of right view; giving to a hundred persons of right view is not equal to giving to a single *srotāpanna*;
giving to a single *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to a hundred *srotāpannas*; [giving to] a hundred...
Giving to one *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to one *anāgāmin*; giving to one *anāgāmin* is not equal to giving to one hundred *anāgāmins*;
giving to one hundred *anāgāmins* is not equal to giving to one *arhat*; giving to one *arhat* is not equal to giving to one hundred *arhats*;
giving to one hundred *arhats* is not equal to giving to one *pratyekabuddha*. One *pratyekabuddha*...
Awakening is not equal to giving to a hundred pratyekabuddhas; giving to a hundred pratyekabuddhas is not equal to giving to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha;
giving to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is not equal to giving to the Buddha and the great assembly of bhikṣus who follow him;
and giving to the Buddha and the great assembly of bhikṣus who follow him is not equal to giving to all those in the four directions.
Giving alms-food to all the bowl-holding monks of the four quarters is not as meritorious as giving a monastery garden to all the monks of the four quarters;
giving a monastery garden to all the monks of the four quarters is not as meritorious as giving a vihāra to all the monks of the four quarters,
for the fruit and retribution obtained from the latter surpasses that of the former.
The Buddha said, “Householder!
That Mīḷhama’s practice of giving is not equal to that of someone who gives food and drink to a single person of right conduct.”
When seeing people, giving to one person of right view is not as meritorious as giving to a hundred persons of right view;
giving to a hundred persons of right view is not as meritorious as giving to one *srotāpanna*; giving to one *srotāpanna* is not as meritorious as giving to a hundred *srotāpannas*;
giving to a hundred *srotāpannas* is not as meritorious as giving to one *anāgāmin*; giving to one *anāgāmin* is not as meritorious as giving to a hundred *anāgāmins*.
One hundred *anāgāmins* are not equal to giving to one *arhat*; one *arhat* is not equal to giving to one hundred *arhats*;
one hundred *arhats* are not equal to giving to one *pratyekabuddha*; one *pratyekabuddha* is not equal to giving to one hundred *pratyekabuddhas*;
and one hundred *pratyekabuddhas* are not equal to giving to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha.
Giving to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha who has attained equal enlightenment is not as meritorious as giving to the Buddha and the great community of bhikṣus following him;
giving to the Buddha and the great community of bhikṣus following him is not as meritorious as giving food to all the bowl-holding monks of the four quarters;
and giving food to all the bowl-holding monks of the four quarters is not as meritorious as giving to a single [monk] of the four quarters...
Giving all monastic groves to the Sangha of the four directions is not as meritorious as giving all monasteries to the Sangha of the four directions;
giving all monasteries to the Sangha of the four directions is not as meritorious as dedicating one’s heart with resolve to take refuge in the Buddha,
Dharma, and Sangha for as long as one lives— the resulting retribution of the latter surpasses that of the former.
The Buddha said, “Householder!
That Mīḷhama’s practice of giving is not equal to that of someone who gives food and drink to a single *samyak* [righteous person].”
Regarding the sight of persons: giving to one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred persons of right view;
giving to a hundred persons of right view is not equal to giving to one *srotāpanna*; giving to one *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to a hundred *srotāpannas*;
giving to a hundred *srotāpannas* is not equal to giving to one *anāgāmin*; giving to one *anāgāmin* is not equal to giving to a hundred *anāgāmins*.
One hundred *anāgāmins* are not equal to giving to one *arhat*; one *arhat* is not equal to giving to one hundred *arhats*;
one hundred *arhats* are not equal to giving to one *pratyekabuddha*; one *pratyekabuddha* is not equal to giving to one hundred *pratyekabuddhas*;
one hundred *pratyekabuddhas* are not equal to giving to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Giving to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha who has attained equal enlightenment is not as meritorious as giving to the Buddha and the great community of bhikṣus following him;
giving to the Buddha and the great community of bhikṣus following him is not as meritorious as giving food to all the bowl-holding monks of the four quarters;
and giving food to all the bowl-holding monks of the four quarters is not as meritorious as giving to a single [monk] of the four quarters...
Giving all monastic groves to the Sangha of the four quarters is not as meritorious as giving all monasteries (vihāras) to the Sangha of the four quarters;
giving all monasteries to the Sangha of the four quarters is not as meritorious as dedicating one’s mind with sincerity throughout one’s life to take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha;
and dedicating one’s mind with sincerity throughout one’s life to take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha is not as meritorious as [not killing] throughout one’s life.
“Abstaining from killing, abstaining from stealing, abstaining from sexual misconduct, abstaining from false speech, and abstaining from drinking intoxicants—
the karmic fruits obtained from these are superior to the previous fruits.
Thus spoke the Buddha.
“Householder! That Mīḷhama’s practice of giving is not equal to someone giving food and drink to a single person of right view;
one person of right view is not equal to giving to a hundred persons of right view; a hundred persons of right view are not...”
Just as giving to one *srotāpanna* is not equal to giving to one hundred *srotāpannas*,
giving to one hundred *srotāpannas* is not equal to giving to one *anāgāmin*, giving to one *anāgāmin* is not equal to giving to one hundred *anāgāmins*,
and giving to one hundred *anāgāmins* is not equal to giving to one *arhat*. Giving to one *arhat* is not...
Just as giving to one hundred arhats is not equal to giving to one pratyekabuddha; giving to one pratyekabuddha is not equal to giving to one hundred pratyekabuddhas;
giving to one hundred pratyekabuddhas is not equal to giving to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha;
and giving to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is not equal to giving to the Buddhas and those who follow the Buddhas.
O bhikṣus, giving food to the Buddha and the great assembly of bhikṣus following him is not as meritorious as giving food to all the bowl-holding monks of the four quarters;
giving food to all the bowl-holding monks of the four quarters is not as meritorious as giving [a gift] to all the monasteries of the four quarters.
Giving to all the monasteries and groves of the fourfold assembly is not as meritorious as giving to all the vihāras of the fourfold assembly;
giving to all the vihāras of the fourfold assembly is not as meritorious as dedicating one’s heart with resolve to take refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha for as long as life lasts;
dedicating one’s heart with resolve to take refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha for as long as life lasts is not as meritorious as refraining from taking life for as long as life lasts.
Not stealing, not engaging in sexual misconduct, not speaking falsehoods, and not drinking intoxicants;
throughout one's entire life refraining from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and drinking intoxicants—
this is not as meritorious as a person who, throughout all places in the worlds of the ten directions, practices great loving-kindness and benefits all sentient beings.
"Birth is free from all conceptualization because the mind is signless; therefore, the retribution obtained is superior to previous retributions.
When the World-Honored One had finished speaking these words, he addressed the elder, saying:
"The Brahmin Mīḷha who performed the great sacrificial assembly in the past was none other than myself, among the various śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas."

When the householder Anāthapiṇḍada had heard the Buddha’s teaching, he was free from the view of a self, the view of a person, the view of a sentient being, and the view of a life-span; having distanced himself from deluded conceptions, his mind attained purity, and he realized the patience of cessation.
The Sūtra on the Elder’s Reward for Giving Spoken by the Buddha
